summary.headline: RSWM Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.7% QoQ to ₹1,161 crore and EBITDA to ₹94 crore (8.0% margin), led by a 39.8% gross margin.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was ₹1,161 crore, up 1.7% QoQ, with domestic sales up to ₹825 crore and exports down to ₹336 crore. Gross margin expanded to 39.8% from 37.4%, lifting EBITDA to ₹94 crore (+10.1% QoQ, +16.1% YoY) and margin to 8.0%. PAT was ₹17 crore against ₹7 crore a year ago, but lower than Q4 FY26, which included a one-time tax benefit. Management gave no full-year guidance; fabric profitability weakened sharply while yarn held up, and new projects (PET food-grade chips, denim garmenting JV, knitting expansion) were outlined.

segments.name: Yarn (synthetic, cotton, mélange)
segments.commentary: Utilisation was about 96% for synthetic, 98% for cotton and 92-93% for mélange. Management said yarn demand held up and cotton/mélange spreads were good in Q1; Q2 is running similarly so far.

segments.name: Denim fabric
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation was about 90%. Management said the segment faced the same cost and demand pressure as knit, with exports and domestic roughly balanced.

segments.name: Knit fabric
segments.commentary: Utilisation was in the mid-80s%. Fabric EBIT was close to nil in Q1 and was negative (about ₹2 crore) in Q4 FY26, versus about ₹35-36 crore last year, as export garmenters' demand was subdued.

guidance_outlook: No full-year growth or EBITDA margin guidance given; management said all quarters should be similar to or better than Q1.

Power cost savings of about ₹40 crore for FY27 at constant utilisation (from renewables and efficiency), with a stated target of around ₹100 crore; renewable share of power rose from mid-20s% to mid-40s%, and about 60% in the current quarter.
Management expects per-unit power cost to fall by more than ₹1 year-on-year on average.
Knitting expansion expected to add benefits from Q3 FY27, with capacity going from 650 tons to about 900 tons per month, including 150 tons of printing.

Food-grade PET chip plant: completion in Q4 FY27, trials and commercial production in Q1 FY28; 50,000 tpa capacity, ₹500 crore revenue expected, about 15% EBITDA (industry norm per management). Utilisation ramp of 75%, 85%, then 90-91% over three years.
Graphene-based fibre (with Birla Cellulose): management expects commercial traction within FY27.
risks_watch: Crude and polyester price volatility, and a possible reversal of Q1 stocking gains.
Export demand recovery, especially knit fabric and Middle East markets; the company said recent inquiries are improving.
Fabric margins near nil; monitor whether fabric EBIT recovers in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
PET plant execution: food-grade certification and trials, no customer tie-ups yet, and a 15% EBITDA assumption that is management's industry norm.
Garmenting JV: stake and capex undisclosed, new skills needed, and a labour-intensive business that is new to RSWM.
Finance costs rising with working capital needs (₹31 crore).
Management gave no full-year guidance; the company's disclosure is limited on volumes and capex amounts.
Investor-presentation timing: it was uploaded about 15 minutes before the call, which an analyst objected to.

qa_highlights.question: What is the update on the graphene-based fibre initiative with Birla Cellulose, when will it generate revenue, and what is the addressable market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the project is ongoing with positive trial judgements and a first product round received from Grasim/Birla Cellulose; it expects it to start rolling within FY27. No market-size estimate yet; it will first master the product and then assess applications.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give yarn and fabric volumes and price movements for the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not disclose tonnage or metres. It gave utilisation: synthetic yarn ~96%, cotton ~98%, mélange 92-93%, denim ~90%, knit mid-80s%, and said polyester prices rose up to 30% in March, with stabilisation since.

qa_highlights.question: What is the stake, capacity and timing for the denim garmenting JV, and will it use internal fabric?
qa_highlights.answer: Stake still under discussion, with RSWM as major majority holder; phase 1 up to 5 lakh pieces per month, with two further phases. It is not a captive line; internal and external fabric will compete on price and quality. Knit garmenting may come in phase 2 or 3.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any tie-up with customers for the food-grade PET chip plant, and what are its revenue and margin assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no customer tie-ups yet. Capacity is 50,000 tpa, expected revenue ₹500 crore, and industry EBITDA of about 15%. Completion is planned in Q4 FY27 with commercial production in Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is there full-year growth or margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance given. Management said Q1 performance was positive, with cash profit up about 12% QoQ and EBITDA of ₹94 crore (about 8%), and expects all quarters to be similar to or better than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why is fabric EBIT close to nil versus ₹35-36 crore last year, and is there a transfer-pricing change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to subdued knit demand, cost pressure, and export garmenter weakness, not transfer pricing. Denim is balanced across export and domestic, while knit is mostly export-dependent. Inquiries have improved for the last two months. Yarn did better because yarn demand held up.

qa_highlights.question: How much power cost reduction is expected, and by how much per unit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said renewables and efficiency gave a visible ~10% cut in power and fuel QoQ (₹123 crore to ₹112 crore). It targets about ₹40 crore in FY27 savings at constant utilisation, with a total target of around ₹100 crore. Per-unit power cost is expected to fall by more than ₹1 YoY on average.

qa_highlights.question: What PET plant utilisation ramp is planned, and what is the knit expansion benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: PET utilisation: 75% in year 1, 85% in year 2, and 90-91% by year 3. Knit capacity rises from 650 to about 900 tons per month, including 150 tons of printing, with benefits expected from Q3 FY27.

capex_capacity: Knitting expansion: capacity going from about 650 tons to about 900 tons per month, including 150 tons of printing capacity that does not exist today; benefits expected from Q3 FY27 via trials then scale-up.

Food-grade PET chip (B2B) plant: civil construction under way and orders placed for critical machines; completion in Q4 FY27, trials and commercial production in Q1 FY28; capacity 50,000 metric tons per year; expected revenue ₹500 crore; industry EBITDA norm about 15%.
PET plant utilisation ramp: 75% in year 1, then 85%, then 90-91% by year 3; certifications and trials required as food-grade product.

Denim garmenting JV: board gave principal approval on the day of discussion; stake percentage still under discussion but RSWM to be major majority shareholder; phase 1 up to 5 lakh pieces per month, with two further phases planned; denim first, knit possibly in phase 2 or 3.

Power cost: about ₹40 crore savings for FY27 at constant utilisation; company targeting around ₹100 crore total; renewable share of power up from mid-20s% to mid-40s%, about 60% in current quarter; power and fuel ₹112 crore vs ₹123 crore in Q4 FY26.
Graphene-based fibre with Birla Cellulose: first product round from Grasim/Birla Cellulose received; management expects it to start rolling within FY27; no capex or market-size figure disclosed.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 was volatile: crude-linked polyester fibre prices rose up to about 30% in March, hurting volumes in April-June; customers bought only as needed (lowest stocking), so business was mainly fresh lifting.
Prices have stabilised somewhat by the call date but crude volatility persists; domestic demand was less volatile than international demand.
Synthetic yarn: reasonably good sales in Q1, and Q2 running similarly so far. Cotton and mélange yarn: Q1 was good due to yarn-cotton spread and stocking gains; Q2 reasonably good so far.

Fabric: knit demand subdued as export garmenters (most knit customers) operated at low production; cost pressure from fibre, gas, freight and chemical prices. Denim is roughly balanced between export and domestic. Management said the last two months saw positive demand and a lot of inquiries.

Export revenue fell QoQ to ₹336 crore; management confirmed export weakness drove the lack of top-line growth, citing West Asia conflict, long transit times and high freight. Middle East demand subdued in the quarter.
Management said it could not give volumes in tonnes or metres; utilisation given instead: synthetic yarn ~96%, cotton ~98%, mélange ~92-93%, denim ~90%, knit mid-80s%.
key_quotes: So, thereby, in synthetic yarn business, RSWM could do reasonably good sales in this quarter, and the current quarter is also going in more or less the same way.
We have not done any tie-up at this point of time.
So, 75, 85 and then probably up to 90, 91%.
I expect it will be anything more than ₹1 per unit on an average year-over-year basis because of the impact of all these renewable sources we are using.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the power-cost and PET plans, but cautious and evasive on forward numbers: management declined full-year guidance, did not give volumes or capex amounts, and attributed the weak fabric margin to external conditions.

adds.what: Knitting expansion: capacity from ~650 to ~900 tons/month, incl. 150 tons printing
Food-grade PET chip plant, 50,000 tpa (~₹500 cr revenue expected)
Denim garmenting JV, phase 1 up to 5 lakh pieces/month (stake still under discussion)

growth.why: No full-year growth guidance; Q1 revenue rose only 1.7% QoQ with exports falling, but knitting expansion (Q3 FY27), a PET plant (Q1 FY28) and a denim JV are lined up, and management says all quarters should be similar to or better than Q1.
